exercise1.prompt: A date read from a file is text until you say otherwise.

hiddenCases.name: a single date is its own earliest
dates across a year boundary are ordered by time
the text is parsed into real dates

exercise1.hint: Parse first, then take the minimum, then format it back. On ISO-formatted text the alphabetical answer happens to agree, which is exactly why the habit matters when the format changes.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with comparing dates as text?
choices: It compares character by character, so the order is only right for some formats
questions.explain: ISO dates happen to sort correctly as text. "01/03/2024" does not, and nothing tells you which kind you have.

questions.prompt: What does parse_dates on read_csv do?
choices: Converts those columns to datetimes as the file loads
questions.explain: It does the conversion at load time, so there is no window in which the column is text and someone sorts it.

questions.prompt: What does .dt give you on a datetime Series?
choices: Date parts and formatting for every value at once
questions.explain: year, month, day, weekday and strftime, applied across the whole column -- the datetime counterpart of .str.
